title: Fine-Grained Japanese Clinical Named Entity Recognition: A Controlled Comparison of BERT and Open-Weight Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2611.22219v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Background: Generative large language models (LLMs) offer an alternative to encoder-based clinical named entity recognition (NER), but their performance on fine-grained Japanese extraction tasks and sensitivity to generation settings remain uncertain. Methods: We compared two fine-tuned BERT-CRF baselines with nine open-weight LLMs on iCorpus, which defines 113 entity categories. The evaluation used 433 sentences from 36 test documents; 1,672 sentences were used for training. LLMs were evaluated using zero-shot prompting with and without JSON Schema constraints and three-seed QLoRA fine-tuning. Fine-tuned models were assessed under different output-token limits, including 900 and larger model-specific limits of 2,600 or 4,096 tokens. Performance was measured using sentence-level label-surface matching with relaxed and exact-surface F1. Results: The highest zero-shot relaxed F1 was 0.337, compared with 0.836-0.841 for the BERT baselines.

translated_title: 细粒度日语临床命名实体识别：BERT与开放权重大型语言模型的受控比较
translated_abstract: 背景：生成式大型语言模型（LLM）为基于编码器的临床命名实体识别（NER）提供了替代方案，但其在细粒度日语抽取任务上的性能以及对生成设置的敏感性仍不确定。方法：我们在定义了113个实体类别的iCorpus语料库上，将两个经过微调的BERT-CRF基线模型与九个开放权重的大型语言模型进行了比较。评估使用了来自36个测试文档的433个句子；1,672个句子用于训练。大型语言模型通过有无JSON Schema约束的零样本提示以及三次随机种子的QLoRA微调进行评估。微调后的模型在不同的输出token限制下进行评估，包括900以及更大的模型特定限制（2,600或4,096个token）。性能通过句子级标签-表层匹配进行测量，采用宽松表层F1和精确表层F1。结果：零样本设置下最高的宽松表层F1为0.337，而BERT基线模型达到0.836-0.841。
tldr: 在包含113个实体类别的细粒度日语临床命名实体识别任务中，微调的BERT-CRF基线模型（F1达0.836-0.841）显著优于开放权重大型语言模型（零样本最高F1仅0.337）。
en_tdlr: Fine-tuned BERT-CRF baselines (F1 0.836-0.841) substantially outperform open-weight LLMs (best zero-shot F1 0.337) on fine-grained Japanese clinical named entity recognition with 113 entity categories.
